exercises.title: Emerging Electronics and Capstone Integration: engineering judgment
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Which approach best demonstrates sound judgment when working with GaN?
choices: State assumptions, calculate a bounded expectation, check ratings, and verify with a safe measurement
Use the typical value as a guarantee and increase power until the expected result appears
Replace components at random before documenting the original symptom
hints: The strongest answer preserves safety, assumptions, limits, and evidence.

exercises.title: Emerging Electronics and Capstone Integration: worked analysis
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Defend a capstone architecture and one emerging technology choice using a weighted decision matrix.

Show assumptions, equations, units, standard-value choices, ratings, tolerance effects, and the measurements that would verify the result.
checklist: I drew or described the complete source and return path.
I carried units and checked the order of magnitude.
I checked ratings and at least one worst-case condition.
I wrote an observable verification step before viewing the solution.
hints: Start with a symbolic relationship before substituting numbers.
Separate typical behavior from guaranteed limits and add measurement tolerance.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference solution

Use a weighted decision matrix with requirement-linked criteria such as efficiency, voltage/current capability, switching frequency, thermal path, availability, cost, tooling, maturity, EMI risk, and safety evidence. Normalize scores, perform sensitivity analysis on weights, and document vendor claims that still require prototype verification. Novelty is justified only by measurable system benefit.

The governing principle is: **compare emerging technology against cost, maturity, safety, supply, tooling, and measurable system benefit**. Define every reference direction and convert values to coherent SI units. Compare the result with component ratings and standard available values, then report a bounded expectation that includes tolerance, temperature, supply variation, and instrument loading.

### Verification evidence

1. Power off and confirm wiring, polarity, and discharge state.
2. Configure a conservative current limit.
3. Predict source current and the critical node voltages or waveform features.
4. Power on and compare the first measurement with the bounded prediction.
5. Stop if current, temperature, smell, or waveform exceeds the safe bound.

The notebook should make both the reasoning and bench test independently reproducible.

exercises.title: Emerging Electronics and Capstone Integration: measurement and fault investigation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Plan or perform a low-voltage investigation of **novelty chosen without requirement, vendor claim unverified, integration risk hidden, safety case incomplete**. Record a safe setup, predicted healthy evidence, observed evidence, one hypothesis at a time, and the final verification.
checklist: I documented the de-energized inspection and safe current limit.
I recorded expected healthy readings before measuring.
I used one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.
I included final evidence that distinguishes cause from symptom.
hints: Measure the supply current and block boundaries before probing internal details.
Change only one condition between measurements.

exercises.title: Diagnosable connected embedded system
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Complete the phase project **Diagnosable connected embedded system**. Produce requirements, safety limits, calculations, schematic or block diagram, component choices, test plan, measured or simulated evidence, fault analysis, and a concise design review.
checklist: Requirements and pass criteria are measurable.
Safety, power, thermal, and interface limits are documented.
Calculations and component selections cite evidence.
The test plan includes nominal, boundary, and fault cases.
Results include annotated diagrams or waveforms and a revision note.
hints: Freeze measurable requirements before selecting components.
Review the current loops, return paths, fault states, and test access before layout or assembly.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference project standard

A passing project is not defined by matching one exact circuit. It is defined by traceable requirements and evidence. The reference architecture separates source protection, power conversion, sensing, control, interfaces, and loads. Each block states input/output ranges, safe states, and test points.

The calculation package includes nominal and worst-case values, power and thermal budgets, tolerance effects, and component-rating margins. The verification matrix maps every requirement to a test or inspection with objective pass criteria. The troubleshooting section includes at least one injected open, short or bias fault and the measurements that isolate it.

A strong submission also records a discovered weakness and the revision made in response; engineering quality is demonstrated by the feedback loop, not by pretending the first version was perfect.

exercises.title: Final Electronics Engineering Capstone
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Design and defend a substantial low-voltage electronic system integrating analog sensing, embedded control, communications, protected power, PCB considerations, diagnostics, and objective verification. Include requirements, safety analysis, calculations, schematic, simulations, firmware architecture, layout review, measurements, fault injection, and revision history.
checklist: Every requirement maps to objective verification evidence.
The safety, power, thermal, interface, and fault-state analyses are complete.
Schematics, simulations, firmware, and layout decisions are mutually consistent.
Bring-up and troubleshooting records include annotated measurements.
The design defense states limitations, residual risks, and next revisions.
hints: Choose a problem whose requirements can be measured with available low-voltage equipment.
Freeze interfaces and power budgets before detailed schematic and firmware work.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Capstone reference standard

There is no single correct product, but there is a correct evidence structure. The reference submission contains measurable requirements, a block diagram with interface ranges, a complete power and energy budget, worst-case analog calculations, protected external interfaces, deterministic firmware states, an offline-safe communications policy, reviewed return paths and decoupling, and a verification matrix.

Bring-up proceeds rail by rail under current limit, then clock/reset, programming, static I/O, sensors, actuators, and communications. Each stage has expected readings and a stop condition. Fault injection demonstrates recovery from a disconnected sensor, shorted output or communication failure without unsafe behavior. The final defense distinguishes verified facts, simulations, assumptions, and work still required for certification or high-energy use.
